Also, like 70% of the passives for Relics (the items that you earn from runs and use to empower your next ones) are 'duds' that don't really do much for you. Start with throwing knives? +3 into a stat (equaling like a 1% power gain at lvl 1)? Yeah, garbage.

Also only one person being able to work on story progress per round is insanely dumb. 

Definitely a lot of room for improvement but what you get is a really fun romp through Elden Ring in a very condensed ~30-45 minute run.

This review was made after 77 hours and getting all Steam achievements.

Elden Ring: Nightreign is a solid game and a departure from the typical souls style rpg. This game puts you under strict time pressure, throws curveballs at you, and challenges your ability to make quick decisions. This game is not beginner friendly and I would not recommend it as your first souls experience. If you're considering playing this and have not played a souls game I would recommend you try out Elden Ring first so you can have a much more gradual ease into the stat system and combat. However if you're a souls vet then this is definitely worth considering as a game that will test you in a variety of ways.

The gameplay loop is relatively simple. You have 2 full days of exploring the world to gather exp and items. Then you face a boss each night followed by a final boss after the night 2 boss. The shrinking zone forces you to clear camps quickly while also trying to loot. 

The combat is extremely well done since it is basically just a Elden Ring spinoff. There was a surprising amount of changes to weapon animations and movement potential that speed up the gameplay.

The night 3 bosses are all pretty unique and well designed. Each has an element or type weakness that is shown to you before you start your run so you should be on the lookout for weapons or spells/incantations of that type during your days exploring.

The playable characters all have unique stat spreads and often have a unique moveset for their favorite weapon type. They all come with a passive, an ability, and an ultimate. Each one plays differently and brings a good amount of variety as well as depth to mastering the game. 

The issues with the game: 

Lack of communication between teammates can be frustrating since this is such a fast paced environment and simply walking off a ledge can lead to a huge time loss. This is also an issue with sharing loot as it can be hard to tell which teammate to grab an item. It currently is a generic marker and players do not have a way to say "ok" or "no" in response to a suggested pickup. 

Variety between runs is a bit lacking currently with only a few ways the map is modified each run or in game events that occur usually on day 2. The current in game events do not feel fairly balanced and some are really helpful while others are just a pain and can end runs. 

There are also a few world bosses like the death bird that are a bit over tuned and you need to be level 12+ to take on safely.

It does not take long for a player to discover every possible upgrade they can get from a boss drop. These can sometimes even be hindrances if taken like the one that converts flask healing to be healing over time which tends to be worse in most situations. It would be nice if a bit more variety was added to these that aren't just stat increases. Lightning when dodging is a really solid example of a minor buff that can change the way you play the game. I would really like to see more examples of these types of modifiers that can change how you play.

Relics are a really interesting concept but sadly their current implementation feels very unrewarding and way too grindy. These add pre game modifiers to your character and can have up to 3 buffs per relic. The main problem is that the relics (other than boss and character quest) are randomly generated at the end of each of your runs. You can end up getting a 3 sized relic with 3 buffs that do not work together at all and it just feels like a waste of space. Possible improvements to this system could be more relics per run so you get more chances at better relics, a system to breakdown and combine relics, or just an overhaul of the relics so they always provide better stats/ character modifiers.

Overall:

 Elden Ring: Nightreign is a solid roguelike coop experience that is optimally played with 2 friends on a call.  There is enough of a game here to keep you interested for about 60 hours which is low for a roguelike but decent for the price. I'll return to this review once more content is added.

Okay, I want to write a little Review here because I was positively surprised with Elden Ring: Nightreign (didn't expected that to be honest, I kept my expectations in check).
Before I start, here a few stats: 

- Steam says it took me 23 hours to roll Credits 
- In Game it says 20:26:12 and 13:23:23 Expedition Time
- Played 22 Expeditions
- 8 Wins
- 3 Streak
- 22 times with Wylder, 0 with any other character
- defeated every Nightlord once
- 29/37 Achievements at the time of writing this

Just wanted to give you a glimpse so you know where I'm coming from. Usually I review a Game after finishing it (well, technically I did finish it once but I will definitely play way more) or 100%ing it but I think since this is not the usual type of Game we get from FromSoft I can make an exception here.
There is still much to do for me. Playing and learning all the other characters, get all the Outfits, finish up the Achievements that are missing, playing with friends, learning more about the Game, do all the Remembrances and just having more fun with this in general.

I could've probably wrote to a few people out of my friendslist but 99% I played with randoms and only 2-3 times I tried a solo expedition.
First off, solo wasn't fun for me. Even as a Souls(-like)/FromSoft Veteran you will have a hard time. It is definitely possible but it wasn't really fun for me. Usually I like going solo, not here though.
But with randoms it was way more fun than I expected. Sure, it is probably best played with your friends, but 90% of the time I had a good experience with random people.
I also have to admit that the first few runs I didn't know what was going on. It was frantic. I was running around like a headless chicken. Sure, in combat I held my own and I learned my character but in regards of where to go, what to prioritize!? This can be overwhelming in the beginning because it really is that fast paced. Time is runes, runes is level ups, gotta run, gotta go fast, zoom from one objective to the next.
I kind of expected it to be bad or annoying. But it wasn't. I really was having fun here and this was extremely surprising in a good way.
Also it helped to play with a few people who were a bit more "experienced" in Nightreign because they probably played since the beginning and/or watched some guides, so at the beginning I hoped for people pinging on where to go and it payed out, because they did.

Performance wise the Game runs buttery smooth for me (i5-13600k, 3060Ti, 32GB RAM, installed on a SSD and I have defect fans so my PC gets kind of hot in some Games, but not here) BUT there was one issue that was really, REALLY annoying. In some Bossfights/Areas the Game would freeze randomly between 3-20 seconds. I read it has probably something to do with Multithreading?! Don't know, but this was the only thing that I didn't like at all.

So yeah, I really had/have fun with Elden Ring Nightreign and I think it deserves better, so I wanted to give my 2 cents here.
Since I don't want to write a novel this time I will just check out here and jump right back into the Game...

If you are unsure of buying it but you love FromSoft, this is 40€/$ and you can have a great time with it if you just allow it. 

Recommended!

Edit: I don't know what happened. Right after "finishing" the Game I went right back in to try out another character. Been playing him since 20 Matches but after my Review the Matchmaking experience became horrible. From those 20 Matches as of writing this I only finished 4 Expeditions. Either people don't ping and run all over the place or don't listen to pings at all. Match Compositions also got worse. Also, when 2 people leave, I shouldn't be penalized if I also want to next. Maybe I got unlucky. I will still keep playing but man this is frustrating... Game still good though.

Edit2: Jeez, I don't know what's going on but matchmaking is getting worse. I feel I get matched with people who never played a Videogame before and have zero awareness. Pings get ignored, I don't get picked up, people admiring the scenery, people die in 1 hit because they don't follow for leveling, me doing many bosses solo until I need a team because of the scaling but everyone runs off on their own but without pings of their own. Even though I had some really cool Expeditions with randoms, right now it is a terrible experience. Still doesn't matter that much for me since I will start playing with friends in the next days. But yeah, I'd just say that you should also do the same.

Edit3: The last one, I swear. So after ~98 hours, 100% Achievements, mastering 4 Characters and learning the ins and outs of the other available 4 (also playing with friends and with randoms enough) nothing has changed. I still want to play more and this is unusual. I really hope for more content other than bosses and Nightfarers. This is actually great and I kind of love it.

LASTLAST Edit (this time for real): So, after nearly 170 hours and 203 Expeditions, after mastering every single class (that of course includes all remembrances, killing all bosses multiple times with every single class and of course doing the Everdark Sovereign boss) and getting all skins for everyone it is still fun. I just wanted to say that there is some kind of secret sauce here and I don't know what exactly it is. But this Game deserves at least a Very Positive Rating (as of writing this it sits at mostly positive). Sure, some random matches can be frustrating with people leaving or people not being good at the Game, but the more you play, the more you will also have awesome Expeditions where people (or you) can come in clutch. Oh, and also my Game doesn't freeze at all anymore. Guess they fixed that. So yeah, just wanted to update here. Peace out.

After 90 hours of gametime, getting all achievements and beating all nightlords solo and with trios, I can probably write a review.

♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I love this game.

Now, don’t get me wrong, it has its flaws, but to be honest I don’t think they’re that consequential. First off, DUOS… I don’t see this game working with a duo mode. With the characters we have now, I simply think we wouldn’t have the same synergy in duos that we have with trios. Each character compliments another, and I feel like their abilities (with a few exceptions like Wylder or Executioner) were all designed to be combined with the abilities of other characters. They could add a duo work, but it simply wouldn’t work as well as the trio system works now. One system that they DEFINETLY need to add though, is voice chat. I think FromSoft is just playing us at this point. We have a game with complex boss designs, a game in which every second matters and you have to make game making decisions… and you have to communicate all that through pings… yeah… now I get that FromSoft may be trying to avoid toxicity, but to be honest, I’d rather be screamed at than hope that my teammates telepathically understand a boss route I came up with by pinging a bunch of locations.

Solo mode is definitely… interesting… after a solid 25 hours, I managed to beat all 8 nightlords solo, and it was definitely fun. However, as a solo player you lack freedom. You have to min max the ♥♥♥♥ out of your gameplay, otherwise you simply wont be a high enough level of have enough flasks to beat the nightlord. Wending Graces are a god-sent though! In the Night Aspect expedition, I managed to collect 5 (One from a merchant, another from a merchant in a town, another 2 from bosses and another from the merchant before the nightlord and I bought a pouch from one of them as well) and that combined with the free revive you get on the new patch barely got me through. Although if you’re not as lucky as I was to get 4 churches to get 8 flasks and get 5 graces, then it’ll probably be hell. Right now, the only characters you can really play solo are Wylder (the character I used) and Executioner. I *LOVE* Wylder’s movement – everything about him is smooth and precise, so I didn’t have to adapt a lot coming from previous FromSoft titles. I also beat one nightlord on the Executioner, and coming from Sekiro I actually managed to parry pretty consistently. Executioner is definitely more fun, although Wylder is more consistent and with the right build and relics has a higher damage output – I think…  The game could definitely use more characters that you can play as a solo, because to be honest I don’t see anyone beating Heolster on Recluse or Revenant. I know it won’t really make sense for them to add solo characters to a co-op game but a single character in the new DLC for us solo players would be nice. They could add some sort of solo buff to specific characters, although I don’t see that happening.

As I mentioned I acquired all achievements - writing this review right after I got the final one – and it was pretty enjoyable. The raid achievements were quite tiring and you basically had to do them solo since sometimes the randoms ruined it, like in the case of the Equilibrious Beast raid where they always *tried* to kill it. The best achievement is definitely the one for beating a nightlord with all 8 characters, it forces you to actually experience the game with all it has to offer lol.

My biggest complaint is the replay value… Ive gotten all achievements and have beaten all bosses multiple times, and until the DLC releases I don’t see myself playing all that much beyond sometimes getting on with my friends and grinding the 290k murk I need to get all the remaining skins I haven’t gotten. Not counting the nightlords, I can safely say I have fought each mini boss and end of night boss in this game at least 6 times, and seeing how most of them are reused from previous games, it gets a bit tedious. Don’t get me wrong, I loved getting my revenge on the Nameless King after Dark Souls 3, but after the 10th time beating him, the hype died down quite a bit. This is clearly just a fun side project for FromSoft, and for what it is its great! However its way smaller than what we have come to expect. Although with that comes the reduced price, so this whole complaint is basically meaningless. I do hope the DLC expands on the game a lot more, and honestly – no matter how unlikely it is – I do hope this will become FromSoft’s live service game, because I’d love to get on once a month or two to try and take on a new nightlord with a new character.

Overall, Elden Ring Nightreign is a VERY strong 8 for me, barely not reaching a 9. If Ishizaki keeps working with FromSoft, Im sure we’ll get a masterpiece from him yet. The game is fun and is definitely worth the price tag. I’d say I’m pretty good at souls games so maybe some people will be able to play this for even longer than I did without having completed all the content. I can’t wait for the expansions!
Fun
